rule.description: A function absorbs the implementation bodies of the sub-methods that used to carry parts of its job: its own body bloats into an extreme measured mass of statements and control-flow decisions that mixes orchestration with low-level detail, and/or the original sub-methods are left declared but unreferenced because every caller now executes the copied bodies.

checks.description: Detect functions whose own body carries an extreme measured mass of statements and control-flow decisions after sub-method implementation bodies were copied into them.
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The function mixes higher-level orchestration with the lower-level implementation that belonged in the absorbed sub-methods; absorption_score (own statements + 2 x own decisions, skipping nested function scope, with JSX-attribute-position arrows attributed to their nearest named enclosing function) reaches 80 or more, more than double the largest value observed anywhere in the clean library (60).

matches.evidence: The keydown handler carries the full tag-commit pipeline inline (candidate validation, editing/limit guards, duplicate suppression, autocomplete resolution with deprecation warning, consumer dispatch, and input/query/selection state resets) plus a second inlined copy of the tag-removal bookkeeping with screen-reader announcements in its backspace branch.

The paste handler inlines the tag-limit guard and input reset, the separator-to-keycode translation copied from a helper exported by the utils module, and a full per-entry copy of the tag-commit pipeline inside its deduplication loop.

checks.description: Detect medium-mass functions whose file simultaneously holds named sub-methods left unreferenced because their callers now execute copied-in bodies.
checks.detected_relation: function -> unreferenced original sub-method in same file
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The copied bodies exist beside their disconnected originals, proving the inlining relation rather than mere incidental length: absorption_score >= 40 with own_statements >= 26 excludes small bookkeeping functions, and at least 2 named functions in the same file have no reference positions in production code (identifier references within the file plus production import sites; member-property positions, non-computed property keys, and the declarations themselves do not count).

matches.evidence: Suggestion commits resolve through an inline copy of the full tag-commit pipeline while the file still declares the original commit method with no remaining production caller.

Rendered tag rows wire their edit-input focus/change/blur, remove-keyboard and click handling through JSX-attribute arrows holding copied-in copies of the shared input and removal handlers, while those shared handlers remain declared in the same file with no production reference.

excluded.reason: The suggestion-list component's render body (E4) also carries absorbed implementation detail (per-suggestion markup assembly, label highlighting, active-row class wiring), and it is part of this case's canonical smell inventory and task scope. However, its measured absorption mass stays near the library baseline because the absorbed markup helpers were small relative to the rendered markup, and its originals were removed rather than left unreferenced, so neither clause of this rule credits it. A size-based detector calibrated to the clean baseline cannot distinguish it from ordinary dense JSX assembling without also flagging unmodified production code; this location is therefore intentionally outside the detection rule and is graded by the task's acceptance boundary rather than by the checker.
